dedupe_keys.name: supplynetpy python library for discrete event simulation of supply chain and inventory networks

description: SupplyNetPy is an open-source Python library for modelling and discrete-event simulation of supply chain networks with arbitrary multi-echelon structures. Users describe a network as a graph of suppliers, manufacturers, distributors and retailers with capacities, costs and replenishment policies, links with costs and stochastic lead times, and demand processes; the library runs the simulation on SimPy and returns logs and node- and network-level performance reports. It supports perishable inventory, node disruptions whose effect on stock can be set (total loss, partial loss and similar), and extension of every component by inheritance. It was written by Tushar Lone, Lekshmi P and Neha Karanjkar and described in an arXiv paper of July 2026 accepted at the Winter Simulation Conference 2026, with validation against analytical benchmarks, a commercial tool and a published case study. It is generic and location independent. The code is free on GitHub and PyPI (pip install supplynetpy, Python 3.9 or later) under the MIT licence; release 0.1.12 appeared on 31 May 2026. Caveats: the library is young (version 0.1), models inventory and flows between nodes, not transport networks or vehicles, and leaves geography to the user. It supports resilience, capacity planning and optimisation studies of logistics chains, including disruption scenarios and supply chain digital twins, and pairs with the GS1 EPCIS event standard catalogued here as a source of observed events.
